messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Protean Systems (private VPC) — NLB target health check failure rate >50% across three AZs. Paging SRE oncall. Severity: P1.

mia (sre-oncall): acked. joining. which tenant pool / dedicated nodes?

zoe (cs): Protean reports lots of 502/timeout from their app. We saw the first spike at ~11:12 UTC. Customer says no recent app deploy.

dan (network): checking NLB -> target group shows unhealthy for majority of targets, healthchecks failing with TCP timeout. No route changes in our control plane. Quick hypothesis: security group change blocked health probes or backend host firewall.

eli (solutions-eng): Protean is on Private deployment (vpc-prod-protean). Last infra change I see was a restrictive SG applied on 11:05 UTC (security lockdown) — could be that. @dan can we confirm which SG attached to targets?

dan (network): confirmed: targets on eni-* have sg-0f3c9b2 (protean-app-sg). Last rule: inbound TCP/443 only from a narrow CIDR (customer ops team). NLB health checks originate from internal LB ENIs, not that CIDR -> probes blocked.

mia (sre-oncall): ok that matches. Impact: 100% of Protean requests are failing to hit healthy targets, so customer-facing outage. Plan: add temp SG rule to allow NLB health check CIDR for 15m, verify healthchecks recover, then remove rule and follow up with customer for permanent fix.

eli (solutions-eng): suggested command to add rule quickly (run from our control plane role):
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0f3c9b2 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.0.0.0/8 --dry-run
# remove dry-run when ready
```

dan (network): will execute patch now (I have AWS console open). I'll add tmp rule for 10.0.0.0/8 (internal region ENIs), annotate change and set a 15m timer.

dan (network): PATCH applied @console - added ingress tcp/443 from 10.0.0.0/8 to sg-0f3c9b2. Marking change id: chg-1758004329-sg-temp.

mia (sre-oncall): watching metrics. healthchecks -> target status flipping to healthy: 11:25 UTC first target, 11:27 majority healthy. Latency/5xx dropping.

zoe (cs): Protean confirms traffic is returning, customers report reduced errors. They want root cause and permanent remediation.

eli (solutions-eng): next steps: 1) coordinate with Protean ops to whitelist NLB probe IPs or widen SG to include our load balancer CIDR; 2) run post-mortem with timeline and repro of the restrictive SG rollout; 3) schedule a hardened healthcheck rule or fallback ALB plan if they prefer app-layer checks.

mia (sre-oncall): setting incident status to "mitigated". I'll leave tmp SG rule in place for 15m, then revert and validate rollback. Logging event and tagging with customer:protean, incident:1758004329.

dan (network): removing temp rule now per timer. Removal done. targets stayed healthy for 5m after revert -> looks stable.

mia (sre-oncall): resolved at 11:40 UTC. filing follow-up runbook with actions: (a) customer SG guidance, (b) add preflight check to our deploy pipeline to detect blocking SGs for private deployments, (c) ops playbook for future quick SG allowance.

incident-bot: Incident 1758004329 status changed -> RESOLVED. Summary: NLB healthcheck failures caused by recently-applied restrictive security group. Temporary ingress rule restored health; permanent remediation planned.
